en.title: Blood Sugar
en.who: Guests who mark sleepy or hungry after meals, sugar cravings, being told their blood sugar is borderline, high blood sugar in the family, belly fat with slim arms, or things changing after 40. Already on blood sugar medication? Everything here goes alongside the doctor, never instead.

say: I hear you. You eat lunch and an hour later you're fighting to stay awake, or you're already hungry again. And once a check-up or a parent's health puts blood sugar on your mind, it's hard to stop thinking about it.
feel.tip: Say back what they marked, in their words. Then ask: "What made you start paying attention: how you feel after meals, a check-up, or your family?"

say: Honestly, I've been there. [Your story in a line or two: when it was, what it felt like, what you tried that didn't work.]
felt.tip: Your own story, or someone close to you ("my dad", "a friend from work"). No story yet? "A lot of the people I talk to say exactly the same thing." Never make one up.

say: What I learned is that for most people the pancreas is still sending insulin, and the cells stopped answering it, usually because of fat around the organs and in the liver. And you don't have to give up rice: change the order you eat in, put protein into breakfast and protect your sleep, alongside your doctor.
So this is what I'd start with.
found.tip: One or two sentences from Part A, then the routine. Pick the products that match what they marked.

en.ask: Based on what you told me, I'd start with protein at breakfast and the Carb Blocker before your rice meals, and keep doing exactly what your doctor tells you. Do you want to take it home tonight?
en.doctor: Very thirsty, peeing a lot, losing weight without trying, blurry vision or cuts that heal slowly? See a doctor first. Already on blood sugar medication? Keep taking it exactly as prescribed, never change it on your own, and tell the doctor before adding anything.
know: The pancreas is usually still sending the signal.

Insulin tells cells to take sugar out of the blood. For most adults over 40 the pancreas is still sending it, often more than ever. The cells stopped answering, like a doorbell nobody comes to, so it rings louder and louder.
Fat in the wrong place is the usual reason.

Fat on the arms is fairly harmless. Fat around the organs and inside the liver drains straight into the liver and keeps it releasing sugar when it should stop. That's why someone a little overweight can have worse numbers than someone much heavier, and why the waist tells you more than the scale.
The order you eat in is free.

Rice and noodles turn into sugar fast, insulin rushes out, and the drop after is the sleepy, hungry-again feeling. Eat vegetables and protein first and the rice last: in trials, the same meal in that order gave a lower curve. Same plate, same person.
You don't have to give up rice.

A plan that asks a family to stop eating rice gets dropped in a week. Flatten the curve on the food they already eat instead: fibre thickens the meal so it empties more slowly, and white kidney bean extract lets part of the starch pass through.
The craving is blood sugar, not willpower.
A carb-only breakfast spikes and then crashes, and when blood sugar drops the brain asks for the fastest fix: more sugar. Protein at breakfast is the single highest-return change in this area.
Muscle is where the sugar goes.

From your 30s you slowly lose muscle unless you use it, and muscle takes up most of the sugar from a meal. Less muscle, less room for sugar. Two strength sessions a week, and enough protein to keep the muscle.
Short sleep raises blood sugar.

Short sleep raises the stress hormone cortisol, cortisol raises blood sugar, and it pushes appetite toward the foods that make tomorrow's numbers worse. A capsule can help you wind down, but it doesn't replace going to bed earlier.
Genes load the dice, they don't roll them.

A lot of what runs in families is shared habits: the same rice, the same late dinners, the same stress. You can't change your genes, but you can start earlier than your parents did and check your numbers every year.
routine: A Plant Protein shake, Double X (or the Men's or Women's Pack) and Advanced Omega
Carb Blocker; no vegetables today? Prebiotic Fiber or Green Superfood in water first
Vegetables and protein first, rice last
Magnesium or Cal Mag D, pick one
Two strength sessions, and the same bedtime every night

zh.title: 血糖管理
zh.who: 适合在问卷里勾了饭后犯困又很快饿、总想吃甜的、体检说血糖临界、家里有人血糖高、四肢不胖肚子大，或者过了40身体变了的客人。已经在吃降糖药的，这里的一切都是配合医生，不是替代。

say: 我懂。中午吃完饭，过一个小时就困得睁不开眼，要不就是又饿了。再加上体检报告上一个数字，或者看到爸妈的身体，心里就一直放不下。
feel.tip: 用对方自己的话，把问卷上勾的说回去。然后问一句：“你是从什么时候开始留意的？是饭后的感觉、体检报告，还是因为家里人？”

say: 说实话，我也经历过。[你的故事，一两句就好：什么时候、什么感觉、试过什么没用。]
felt.tip: 讲你自己的，或者身边人的（“我爸爸”“我一个同事”）。还没有故事？就说：“我身边很多朋友也是这样。”千万别编。

say: 我后来学到，大多数人的胰腺其实还在分泌胰岛素，是细胞不怎么“听”它了，原因通常是脂肪长在了内脏周围和肝里。而且不用戒米饭：换个吃饭的顺序，早餐吃够蛋白质，把觉睡好，同时继续配合医生。
所以，我会先从这个开始。
found.tip: 从 Part A 挑一两句讲，然后讲作息。挑跟对方勾的对得上的产品。

zh.ask: 按你刚才说的，我建议先从早餐的蛋白粉和吃米饭前的阻碳片开始，医生那边该怎么做还是照做。今天要不要先带回去？
zh.doctor: 如果口很渴、小便多、体重莫名下降、视力模糊，或者伤口好得很慢，请先去看医生。已经在吃降糖药的，一定按医嘱继续吃，不要自己调整，添加任何保健品之前先告诉医生。
know: 胰腺通常还在发信号。
胰岛素负责通知细胞把糖从血里搬走。四十岁以上的多数人，胰腺还在发这个信号，往往比以前发得更多，是细胞不再应答了。就像门铃按了没人开，只好越按越用力。
原因通常是脂肪长错了地方。
胳膊腿上的脂肪相对无害；包在内脏周围、长在肝里的脂肪，会直接流进肝，让肝在该停的时候还在往血里放糖。所以有人只是微胖，血糖却比胖很多的人还差，腰围也比体重更能说明问题。
吃饭的顺序是免费的。
米饭面条很快变成糖，胰岛素一下子涌出来，血糖一掉，人就犯困，或者又饿了。先吃菜和肉，最后吃饭：试验里，同一餐换个顺序，血糖曲线就低很多。同一盘菜，同一个人。
不用戒米饭。
要一家人戒掉米饭的方案，一周就会被放弃。不如在本来的饭上把曲线压平：纤维让一整餐变稠、消化得慢，白芸豆提取物让一部分淀粉直接通过。
想吃甜的是血糖，不是意志力。
只有碳水的早餐，血糖先冲高再跌下来，血糖一低，大脑就要最快的补救：再来点糖。早餐吃够蛋白质，是这一块回报最高的一个改变。
饭后的糖，大部分是肌肉消化的。
三十岁以后，肌肉不用就会慢慢流失；肌肉少了，糖就没地方去。每周两次力量训练，再吃够蛋白质，把肌肉留住。
睡不好，血糖就往上走。
睡得少，压力激素皮质醇就升高，血糖跟着升，食欲还会偏向那些让明天指标更难看的东西。胶囊能帮你放松，但代替不了早点上床。
基因决定的是概率，不是结局。
一家人传下来的，还有生活习惯：一样的米饭，一样晚的晚饭，一样的压力。基因改不了，但你可以比父母早一步开始，每年查一次血糖。
routine: 一杯有机植物蛋白粉，加双X（或男士、女士营养包）和深海鱼油
阻碳片；今天没吃到菜，先喝一杯益生元纤维粉或绿色超级食物粉
两次力量训练，每天固定时间睡觉
